newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's CDC watchdog wants cap on budget help.
newsitem.headline: France's CDC watchdog wants cap on budget help.

text.p: The head of the French national assembly committee overseeing the Caisse des Depots et Consignations does not want the government to withdraw more than 13.5 billion francs this year from the state bank to plug budget shortfalls, the Paris business daily La Tribune said.

The newspaper said Jean-Pierre Delalande believed the amount the government could take should be capped at that sum because of the decline in Livret A savings schemes managed by the Caisse de Depots (CDC).

The government, which now is putting the final touches on its 1997 budget to be unveiled in September, has a right to take a share of the profits and reserves of the CDC in return for a state guarantee on the tax-free savings schemes.
Last year, the government took 38.3 billion francs from the CDC to plug a shortfall in its 1995 budget and took a total of 280 billion francs between 1984 and 1994.
The government pledged last year to reduce the amount it takes from the CDC from 1996 onwards because of a fall in savings managed by the bank.
Demand for Livret A savings schemes has fallen in the last few years, hit by strong competition from money market funds and other investment schemes offering higher rates of interest.
The government has already called on the CDC to save beleaguered property lender Credit Foncier, an operation that will cost the state bank 2.5 billion francs.
The government announced last month it had asked CDC to bid for Credit Foncier after it failed to find anyone in the private sector to rescue it from huge losses.
